failure_story: We sized Applied Optoelectronics as a datacenter/800G optics turnaround, leaning on FY2025 revenue growth (+83%) and Q1 2026 datacenter mix (54%) while treating normalized owner cash of $0.74 per share and a component base of ~$15 per share as sufficient downside support at ~$99.77. The investment failed because customer concentration was the binding constraint, not cyclical optics demand: Digicomm (~53%) and Microsoft (~29%) together drove ~82% of FY2025 revenue, and one hyperscaler dual-sourced 800G transceivers at lower price while the other throttled distributor orders. Revenue collapsed faster than the 12% base growth path assumed, CATV Quantum Bandwidth upgrades paused in the same quarter, and Taiwan capacity capex stayed near $179 million (FY2025 actual exceeded $174 million operating cash flow) with operating lease ROU near $72 million still on the books. Equity raises pushed diluted shares from ~60 million to ~76 million, so per-share economics deteriorated even when headline revenue looked stable. The stock re-rated from AI-optics optionality to a concentrated supplier with negative reported free cash flow and unproven moat; total return landed near the bear envelope (-24% per year) rather than the already-negative synthesis base (-13.4% per year), producing severe permanent loss on a small-cap position we should have kept on watch.
